To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the denitrification enzyme apparatus of P. aerugionosa is assembled on the membrane‐bound NO reductase complex and that a flagella protein complex is found in the perplasm of P. aerugionosa.
the denitrification enzyme complex in Pseudomonas is a dynamic protein assembly that is involved in nitrate/nitrite/nitric oxide/nitrous oxide metabolism.

the assembly of a denitrification complex in Pseudomonas is mediated by a stable protein complex composed of four reductase subunits and the maturation factor of nitrite reductases, which serves as a platform for the attachment and maturation of all other denitrification components.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization the assembly and regulation of the denitrifying enzyme complex in P. aeruginos Protein complexes during denitrification of Pseudomonasaeruginosa G. Z
the identification and characterization the protein components of the denitrifying apparatus of Pseudomona aeruginosa.
the identification of the protein components involved in the formation of a multi‐enzyme complex and the determination of the protein–protein interactions that mediate the assembly of this complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interactomics approach is an efficient tool for the elucidation of protein complexes and interactions.
protein complex formation is a prerequisite for the assembly and function in the electron transfer chains during denitrification.

the interactomic analysis of P. aerugiosa denitrification complexes provides an example for how interactomic approaches can be used in the future to study protein complexes in bacteria and to identify the protein components of multi‐enzyme systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the assembly of the entire denitrification machinery in P. aeruginosais mediated by a stable protein–protein complex.
the interactomic analysis revealed a large number of stable and transient interactions between proteins involved in the denitrification process of P. aerugiosa.
protein–protein interactions play a key role in the formation and function of the denitrifying apparatus of P. aerugionsa.
The main takeaway from our work is that
protein complexes are not only involved in energy metabolism but also in many other cellular processes.
the interactomic strategy allows for a detailed characterization of protein–protein interactions and complexes in vivo and in vitro.
the interactome of P. aerugenosa can be considered as a dynamic network of stable and transient interactions that are required for the proper assembly and function of the denitrifying machinery.
